opportunities.title: McKinsey.org Forward learning programme (Fall 2026)
opportunities.overview: Free multi-week online programme teaching practical workplace skills: adaptability, communication, problem-solving, and digital and AI essentials. Applications are open until 5 October.
opportunities.program_dates: Multi-week programme following the application window
opportunities.deadline_text: Applications are open until October 5 (overview page). FAQ: 'Applications for the McKinsey.org Forward program are now open until October 5, 2026. ... in some cases, applications may close earlier than the deadline mentioned above in certain countries.' No time or time zone stated.
funding_details: 'Forward is a free multi-week learning program'
opportunities.participation_fee: None: 'Forward is free for eligible participants ... There are no fees to apply, register, or partake' (official FAQ).
eligibility: Live in a country where Forward is available; the FAQ's Africa list includes the Democratic Republic of the Congo
Working or with prior work experience (including internships or apprenticeships), or preparing to start work in the next 12 months
Less than 5 years of total work experience (exceptions stated for nonprofit, non-corporate or non-managerial roles)
At least a high school education or equivalent
Command of English, French, Brazilian Portuguese, Latin American Spanish or Arabic
opportunities.experience_requirement: Reported: under 5 years of work experience; internships count
opportunities.language_requirement: Primarily English; a secondary source says the digital content is also translated into French
application_process: Apply online from the Forward overview page before 5 October

sources.label: McKinsey.org Forward FAQ (deadline, eligibility, country list, no fees)

opportunities.eligibility_reason: The official FAQ lists the DRC among Forward countries; internships count as prior work experience, total experience is under 5 years, and the course can be followed in English or French.
potential_issues: Deadline is 5 October 2026 (today on re-verification); applications may close earlier in some countries
Missed applicants can only register interest for the next cohort, whose date is not announced
benefits: Skills that employers in the target roles ask for
opportunities.relevance_reason: Free, short and aimed exactly at people starting their career. Problem-solving and digital skills are the gaps that business analyst and operations postings keep naming.
opportunities.action: Apply today if not already done. If the form has closed, register interest on the Forward site for the next cohort.
opportunities.notes: Re-verified 5 October 2026: no extension and no spring 2027 cohort announced. Missed applicants 'can register their interest on the Forward website and will be contacted for the next cohort'.

opportunities.title: Chevening Scholarships 2027/28
opportunities.overview: One-year master's degree at any UK university for emerging leaders. Chevening describes the award as fully funded. The 2027/28 round closes on 6 October 2026.
opportunities.deadline_text: The deadline for applications is 6 October 2026 at 11:00 UTC. You will not be able to access the online application system after this date.
funding_details: Chevening's site states: 'Chevening Scholarships are fully-funded.'
The itemised list (fees, stipend, flights) was not on the pages read on 2 October 2026.
eligibility: At least 2,800 hours of work experience, acquired after completing the undergraduate degree
That experience must be spread over a minimum of two years
Undergraduate degree completed by October 2024 for this cycle
Eligible work: full-time or part-time employment, voluntary work, paid or unpaid internships
nationality_requirements: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has its own Chevening country page and is open for applications
opportunities.age_requirement: Not specified on the pages read
opportunities.experience_requirement: 2,800 hours after the undergraduate degree, over at least two years
application_process: Apply online in the Chevening application system before the deadline
Reading committee assessments from mid-October 2026 to January 2027
Shortlist announced mid-February 2027; interviews March to April 2027
opportunities.eligibility_reason: Chevening requires 2,800 hours of work gained after the undergraduate degree, over at least two years. The recorded profile shows a degree obtained in 2024 and under one year of short internships, so the requirement is not met this cycle.
potential_issues: No UK visa processing centre and no TB testing facility in the DRC: a successful applicant must travel to another country for both
Those trips are paid by the applicant first; reimbursement of some travel costs is discretionary
opportunities.relevance_reason: A strong programme, but the post-degree work-hours rule rules out this round. It becomes realistic once two years of work, volunteering or internships after the degree can be documented.

visa.support: No visa centre in the DRC. Travel to another country to apply; discretionary reimbursement of some travel costs.

opportunities.upfront_cost_risk: Travel to a third country for the visa application and TB test is paid by the applicant before any reimbursement.
opportunities.action: No action this round. Keep a dated log of post-degree work, volunteering and internship hours for a later round.

opportunities.title: Mandela Washington Fellowship for Young African Leaders 2027
opportunities.organization: U.S. Department of State (administered by IREX)
opportunities.overview: Six-week executive-style Leadership Institute at a U.S. college or university in summer 2027 for about 550 young African leaders. Applications are open until 13 October 2026 and there is no application fee.
opportunities.program_dates: Fellowship begins in the United States in June 2027 (six-week institute)
opportunities.deadline_text: APPLICATION DEADLINE: 16:00/4:00 PM GMT on Tuesday, October 13, 2026 (2027 application instructions PDF, still online on 26 October 2026). The About page now says: 'Applications for the 2027 Mandela Washington Fellowship are now closed.'
opportunities.expected_next_cycle: Applications for the 2027 Fellowship closed on 13 October 2026. No 2028 call is announced on the official site (read 26 October 2026).
funding_details: 'If you are selected for the Fellowship, the U.S. Government will cover all program costs' (2027 application instructions)

Listed costs: J-1 visa support; round-trip travel from the Fellow's home city to the United States and domestic U.S. travel as required by the program; a six-week institute; a limited accident and sickness benefit plan; housing and meals during the program; an optional four-week Professional Development Experience (for up to 50 Fellows)
Not covered: salaries while away from work and personal purchases
'There is no fee to apply for the Mandela Washington Fellowship.'
opportunities.participation_fee: None: 'There is no fee to apply for the Mandela Washington Fellowship.'
eligibility: Between the ages of 25 and 35 on or before the application deadline, 'although exceptional applicants ages 21-24 may be considered'
Citizen of an eligible country; the list includes the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)
Resident of an eligible Sub-Saharan African country, permanently residing there as of 1 February 2027 and in June 2027
Not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident; eligible to receive a U.S. J-1 visa
Proficient in reading, writing and speaking English
Selection criteria include a proven record of accomplishment in business, trade, emerging technologies, governance and/or security, and a commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa
nationality_requirements: Democratic Republic of the Congo is on the list of eligible countries
opportunities.age_requirement: 25 to 35 at the deadline; exceptional applicants aged 21 to 24 may be considered
documents_required: Semi-finalists: international passport if available, or other government-issued photo ID, at the Embassy interview
application_process: October 2026 to January 2027: semi-finalists interviewed by U.S. embassies and consulates
February/March 2027: applicants notified of their status
March to May 2027: visa processing and pre-Fellowship activities for finalists
June 2027: Fellowship begins in the United States

sources.label: About the Fellowship ('Applications for the 2027 Mandela Washington Fellowship are now closed.')
2027 application instructions (PDF: deadline, eligibility incl. DRC, financial provisions, timeline)

opportunities.eligibility_reason: DRC citizens living in the DRC can apply and English is at professional level. An applicant under 30 falls within the 21 to 35 range, although below 25 only exceptional applicants are considered. Selection then turns on a proven record of accomplishment.
potential_issues: The track record expected (business, trade, technology, governance or security) is thin on the recorded profile
Nationals of countries under a full or partial U.S. entry or visa suspension can apply, but finalists are selected case by case: check travel.state.gov for the DRC's current status
Finalists need a passport valid through at least 28 February 2028; passport status is not recorded
'J-1 visa support' and a 'limited accident and sickness benefit plan' are the stated visa and insurance terms; no salary replacement
benefits: Six-week institute at a U.S. university
Network of African and American leaders
Possible six-week Professional Development Experience afterwards
opportunities.relevance_reason: The business and governance focus matches the degree and the Ministry internship. The weak point is the leadership record, which the application essays would have to carry.

visa.support: J-1 visa; processing takes place March to May 2027 for finalists.

opportunities.action: Applications for 2027 are closed. If you applied, semi-finalist interviews at the U.S. Embassy run until January 2027 and notifications come in February/March 2027; otherwise watch mandelawashingtonfellowship.org for the 2028 call.
opportunities.notes: 26 October 2026: /apply/, /apply-faqs/ and /2027-application-instructions/ now return HTTP 404 (taken down after the deadline). The About page states that 2027 applications are closed; the instructions PDF is still online and unchanged (deadline, eligibility, DRC on the country list, 'the U.S. Government will cover all program costs', no application fee). The application portal apply.mandelawashingtonfellowship.org still loads a login page. The '2027 Reciprocal Exchange Component' news item (deadline November 11, 2026) is for U.S. professionals, not African applicants.

opportunities.title: Aspire Leaders Program (2026 Cohort 4)
opportunities.overview: Free six-week online leadership programme for first-generation or limited-income university students and graduates aged 18 to 29. Cohort 4 runs from 21 October to 30 November 2026.
opportunities.deadline_text: Cohort 4 (2026): 'Apply before the October 16 deadline' (no time or time zone stated). On 26 October 2026 the programme page lists Cohort 4 'October 21 – November 30' as 'Closed', and the home page says 'Applications for the 2026 Aspire Leaders Program are closed!'
opportunities.expected_next_cycle: Programme page (26 October 2026): '2027' Cohort 1 marked 'COMING SOON' with no dates; home page: 'Check back in for future updates regarding our 2027 program.' The site's Apply button leads to a 2027 interest form; no 2027 application dates or deadline are stated.
funding_details: 'No application fee. No tuition. No catch.'
Free certificate of completion; an optional verifiable e-credential bundle costs USD 5

Programme page lists alumni/graduate support: Skills Advancement Grants (up to USD 200), Community Action Award (up to USD 5,000), Seed Fund, Academic Advancement Grant and Conference Grant (amounts for the last three not stated)
opportunities.participation_fee: None: 'No tuition, no application fee, no cost at any point.' An optional verifiable e-credential bundle costs USD 5; a free certificate is still given.
eligibility: Limited-income or first-generation university students and graduates, anywhere in the world
Currently enrolled in or graduated from an undergraduate or postgraduate university programme
Eligibility is self-identified; no documentation is required (programme page)
application_process: Complete the online application before 16 October 2026
opportunities.eligibility_reason: The age range fits a graduate under 30. The programme is reserved for first-generation or limited-income students and graduates, and the profile does not record either.
potential_issues: Cohort 4 closed on 16 October 2026; 2027 dates not announced
Reserved for first-generation or limited-income applicants
Live sessions need a reliable internet connection
opportunities.relevance_reason: Free, short and built for recent graduates; it also adds a leadership credential that later applications (for example the Mandela Washington Fellowship) look for.
opportunities.action: Cohort 4 is closed. If you are the first in your family at university or come from a limited-income household, watch aspireleaders.org for the 2027 Cohort 1 dates (the site offers a 2027 interest form).
opportunities.notes: Several cohorts run each year. 26 October 2026: Cohort 4 (21 Oct-30 Nov 2026) is marked Closed and the 2027 programme is 'coming soon' with no dates. Eligibility (18-29, enrolled in or graduated from a university programme, limited-income or first-generation) and cost wording ('No application fee. No tuition. No catch.'; optional USD 5 e-credential bundle) unchanged. The feed item 'Aspire Leaders Program 2026' matches this cohort.
